author: bballhaus
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to [#72](https://github.com/bballhaus/civitas/pull/72). Five fixes; the deadline-on-tracker change that was originally in this commit has been **dropped** because [#71](https://github.com/bballhaus/civitas/pull/71) already covers it (and goes further — Q&A deadlines, pre-bid meetings, site visits).

- **RFP detail page took up to ~60s to render** because two LLM endpoints on the critical path were non-streaming: `/api/rfp-requirements-summary` and `/api/capabilities-analysis` each awaited a full ~10–15s Haiku turnaround before returning JSON. Both now stream plain-text chunks (mirroring `/api/match-summary`). First byte typically lands in 200–500ms; all three sections paint in progressively. Updated the four client call sites: `matches/[rfpId]`, `dashboard/rfp/[id]`, and two spots in `dashboard/page.tsx`.

- **Onboarding "Continue" race — chips disappearing on step transition.** Clicking Continue immediately after a NAICS pick refetched the snapshot before the optimistic POST had landed; `setSnapshot` then replaced the just-added chip with stale server state and the chip vanished on the next step. The optimistic commit handler now tracks every in-flight background POST; `goNext` and `finish` call `commitHandler.drainPending()` before refreshing.

- **Progress bar overflow.** The 10 step pips used `overflow-x-auto + shrink-0` so they always horizontally scrolled. Switched to `grid-cols-10` with per-cell `truncate`. All ten pips now fit on one row at any viewport width; long labels like "Certifications" ellipsis-truncate inside their slot, and the leading number collapses on narrow screens (`<sm`).

- **Match-summary truncation.** Bumped `maxTokens` 280 → 500 in `/api/match-summary`. Prompt asks for 1–2 + 2–4 sentences with concrete citations; 280 was tight enough to truncate the second paragraph mid-sentence whenever Haiku included multiple NAICS/capability references. First-byte latency is unaffected (streaming).

- **Score breakdown "not all fields populated on first load"** — investigated; the breakdown is rendered atomically from `data.breakdown` once `/api/match/[rfpId]` resolves, and `matchV2` always returns the 7-category prime breakdown. Rows with `status: "neutral"` intentionally don't show a score number or citation block (no data to cite). With streaming + the onboarding-race fix above, the page should look fully populated on first load. No code change needed for this one.

## Files touched

- `front_end/src/app/api/match-summary/route.ts` — `maxTokens` 280 → 500
- `front_end/src/app/api/rfp-requirements-summary/route.ts` — convert to streaming
- `front_end/src/app/api/capabilities-analysis/route.ts` — convert to streaming
- `front_end/src/app/matches/[rfpId]/page.tsx` — consume both new streams; one onboarding `commitHandler.drainPending()` site
- `front_end/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — consume both new streams
- `front_end/src/app/dashboard/rfp/[id]/page.tsx` — consume both new streams
- `front_end/src/app/onboarding/commit.tsx` — in-flight tracking + `drainPending` on all three handlers (auto / deferred / optimistic)
- `front_end/src/app/onboarding/page.tsx` — `goNext` and `finish` drain before refresh; progress-bar grid layout
- `front_end/src/lib/__tests__/matching-v2.test.ts` — fill in new `RfpCacheRow` key-date columns from PR #71 so the fixture compiles

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (✅ verified locally)
- [ ] `npx tsx --test src/lib/__tests__/matching-v2.test.ts` — 17/17 pass (✅ verified locally)
- [ ] Open an RFP detail page on a fresh profile (no cached match): first byte of each of the three sections (match summary, About this RFP, Capabilities analysis) should appear within ~1s; total to fully-populated should be ~5–15s, not 60s
- [ ] During onboarding, rapidly pick three NAICS rows on the Capabilities step and immediately click Continue — every chip should persist on the next step (and the NAICS step should show the propagated codes)
- [ ] Onboarding progress bar shows all 10 step pips on one row at desktop width without horizontal scroll; cells should ellipsis-truncate if labels get long

Validating A/B/C required real Kite money because paper trading bypassed all the wiring. This PR makes paper a faithful preview while preserving real-money safety semantics.

### Epic A — Paper budget lifecycle (audit-only)

- \`paper/runtime.py\` now fires the full \`reserve() → transition(SUBMITTED) → transition(FILLED)\` lifecycle on every paper fill (3 sites: stop-loss, time-stop, signal). Background daemon thread — never blocks the fill path.

author: ivankuznetsov
body:
## Summary

The bot reads `HIVE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` directly from `ENV` at startup, so the only ways to supply it were a `export` in a shell rc file or a one-off command-line export. After a host reboot or a fresh shell, `hive bot start` would fail with `Hive::ConfigError` until the operator manually re-exported the token.

This PR adds a tiny `Hive::EnvFile` loader and wires it into `hive bot start`. It reads `~/.config/hive/.env` (sibling of `config.yml`) and merges KEY=value pairs into `ENV` without overwriting anything already set.

## Behaviour

- Lives at `~/.config/hive/.env` (XDG config home, honours `HIVE_HOME`).
- Loaded once on `hive bot start`; `hive bot reload` does NOT re-read it (token rotation = full restart).
- `KEY=value` per line. `#` starts a comment. Blank lines ignored.
- Splits on the first `=` only, so values may contain `=` themselves.
- Strips outer `"` or `'` quotes from the value.
- Malformed lines (no `=`, empty key) are silently skipped.
- **Existing ENV vars take precedence.** A manual `export HIVE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=...` always wins.
- Missing or unreadable file is a silent no-op — this is convenience, not a hard requirement.

## Why tiny instead of pulling in dotenv

The format we need is a strict subset of dotenv: no shell expansion, no multi-line values, no `export` prefixes. ~50 lines of pure-Ruby parser is easier to audit than adding a runtime dep with its own changelog and security advisories. Tests cover the eight observable behaviours.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/hive/env_file.rb` | New module. |
| `lib/hive/commands/bot.rb` | Calls `Hive::EnvFile.load!` at the top of `start_bot`. |
| `.gitignore` | Adds `/.env` so a repo-root operator habit doesn't leak the token. |
| `wiki/commands/bot.md` | Documents format, loader, and the rotation-requires-restart rule. |
| `test/unit/env_file_test.rb` | 8 focused tests. |

## Test plan

bundle exec rake test → 3592 runs, 12915 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 2 skips.

bundle exec rubocop --parallel → 419 files, 0 offenses.

Manual smoke: with the token in ~/.config/hive/.env (mode 0600), hive bot start --foreground brings the bot online; the loader hits the new code path and logs nothing extra (silent merge). With the same var pre-set in the shell, the shell value wins (no surprise overrides).

body:
Identified and resolved a performance bottleneck in the showcase rating system. Previously, the application retrieved all rating records for a given subject and calculated the average and count in Python. Additionally, when displaying multiple collections (like on the landing page), it performed a database query for each collection (N+1 problem).

I've optimized this by:
- Using database-level aggregation via SQLAlchemy's `func.avg()` and `func.count()`.
- Introducing a batch retrieval method that fetches all necessary ratings in a single query using `GROUP BY` and the `IN` operator.
- Refactoring the enrichment logic to use this batch method.

The result is a significant reduction in database roundtrips and memory overhead when viewing the landing page or admin collections.

author: mparanzales
body:
## What

Phase 2 of the Supabase migration: the auth flow. Magic-link sign-in, session-refresh middleware, and an anonymous-friendly /profile.

This follows the **Auth Optional** model Maria picked: anyone can browse `/explore`, `/events`, `/venue/[slug]` etc. without signing in. Sign-in unlocks user-scoped persistence (which gets wired up in Phase 3).

## Why

We need real user identity before Phase 3 can move `useSaved` + `useBookings` + profile to Supabase. Without auth, those features stay local-only.

Magic link instead of password because: simpler UX (one tap from email), no password to forget or reset, no leaked-password risk, matches the consumer-app benchmark (OpenTable, Resy, Substack all do this).

## What landed

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/auth.ts` | `getAuthUser()` helper for Server Components |
| `app/(auth)/sign-in/page.tsx` | Server Component, redirects if already authed |
| `app/(auth)/sign-in/sign-in-form.tsx` | Client form, calls `signInWithOtp` with current-origin callback |
| `app/(auth)/auth/callback/route.ts` | Exchanges `?code=` for session, redirects |
| `middleware.ts` | Restored matcher — runs on every non-static request |
| `lib/supabase/middleware.ts` | Refreshes session cookie. **No redirects** (auth-optional). |
| `app/(main)/profile/page.tsx` | Server Component, branches on auth |
| `app/(main)/profile/profile-body.tsx` | Existing UI + Sign Out + anon Sign In CTA |

## How verified

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (typecheck + lint + format)
- [x] `/sign-in` renders form + handles error state (rate limit surfaced as inline message)
- [x] Magic link sent → Supabase OTP endpoint returned 200
- [x] Clicked the link from Gmail → redirected to `/auth/callback` → session cookies set → landed back on `/explore` signed in
- [x] Session persists across full page reloads (middleware auto-refreshes the token)
- [x] `/profile` anonymous view shows the inline sign-in CTA
- [x] `/profile` signed-in view shows the existing profile UI + a sign-out row

## Notes for reviewer

**The "Auth Optional" decision is deliberate.** Earlier discussion (in chat) led Maria to switch from a hard-gate model to auth-optional after reviewing discovery-app benchmarks (Airbnb, OpenTable, Yelp etc. all allow unauthed browsing). The middleware therefore does NOT redirect anonymous users — it just refreshes the session cookie. Individual routes that genuinely need a user (currently only `/profile`) handle the anonymous case inline.

**Phase 3 will:**
- Make `useSaved` + `useBookings` dual-mode (localStorage when anon, DB when authed) with a one-time slug→uuid migration on first sign-in.
- Read profile preferences from `public.profiles.preferences` instead of `MOCK_USER`.
- Wire `/onboarding` to write preferences to the profile row.

**Out of scope:**
- Custom SMTP. Supabase's built-in email service is rate-limited at ~3-4/hour on free tier. We hit it during testing. Before launch, wire Resend ($0 for 3k emails/month).
- Sign-up form. `signInWithOtp({ shouldCreateUser: true })` is the default — first-time emails get a profile row created automatically via the `on_auth_user_created` trigger in `schema.sql`.

Three sets of fixes to resolve deployment errors and improve the student onboarding flow:

### 1. Drizzle ORM: `node-postgres` → `neon-http`

- **`db/user-biometrics.ts`**: Converted raw SQL from `pool.query()` function calls to neon tagged template literals.
- Added `@neondatabase/serverless` as a dependency.

### 2. Set-password flow now supports student number
- **`/api/set-password`**: Accepts either `email` or `studentNumber` to identify the user. Returns the user's email in the response so biometric setup can proceed.
- **`/set-password` page**: Added a student number input field (with an "or" divider before the email field). Reads `?studentNumber=` from URL params.
- **Student login page (`/login/student`)**: Replaced the vague "set your password" text with a prominent "First time logging in? Set up your password" link that passes the entered student number as a query param.

- **Clock-in/clock-out routes**: The previous implementation made internal HTTP `fetch()` calls to `/api/attendance/verify-face` and `/api/attendance/verify-fingerprint` — but these calls didn't forward session cookies, so the biometric endpoints always returned 401 Unauthorized. Fixed by extracting verification logic into `lib/biometric-verify.ts` and calling it directly.
- **Setup-face and setup-fingerprint APIs**: Now accept `studentNumber` as an alternative to `email` for user lookup, ensuring the full set-password → biometrics flow works when a student identifies by student number.

- [ ] **Verify existing email-based set-password still works** — approval emails link to `/set-password?email=...`, confirm this path is unbroken.

author: vedhavyas
body:
`apply_session_update_key_renamed` migrated the bucket from the synth spawn key to whatever `to` the bridge emitted. When Connected fired with an empty `session_id` (the bridge had no real id yet — it picks `resume_id` or empty string), `to` was `SessionKey::from_session_id("")` and the bucket landed at the bare `""` key. Subsequent wire frames with the real session_id couldn't find that bucket and `apply_sdk_message_presentation` dropped them with `sdk_message_dropped` logs — `Result` frames stuck the spinner on "Thinking..." forever; `Assistant` frames orphaned in the background.

A concurrent secondary bug: two empty-Connecteds in a row both targeted the same `""` key, and the `already_under_to` branch silently dropped the second synthetic bucket entirely.

## Fix shape (planner-judgment: symptom patch over source fix)

**1. KeyRenamed handler**: when `to.as_str().is_empty()`, substitute `__pending_<from>__` so the bucket stays at a uniquely identifiable synth key. Two concurrent empty-Connecteds now land in distinct `__pending_<from_a>__` and `__pending_<from_b>__` buckets — no silent drop.

**2. `apply_sdk_message_presentation`**: when the wire session_id doesn't match any known bucket, call `rekey_pending_bucket_to`. If exactly one `__pending_*` bucket exists, rekey it to the wire session_id (mirroring `set_session_id`'s PRE_CONNECT_KEY migration shape) and fall through to the normal routing.

## Design choices

**Symptom patch over source fix**: option (a) from the plan. The cleaner architectural fix is delayed-Connected emission at the bridge layer, but that introduces a "Connecting..." indefinite window for idle new sessions and a deeper test gap. Symptom patch composes with existing bucket-migration machinery and stays within the TUI reducer surface. Filed as a v2 follow-up candidate if the symptom patch turns out wartier in practice.

**Ambiguous-multi-pending case**: when MULTIPLE `__pending_*` buckets exist (concurrent-spawn with different leads, where neither has surfaced a wire frame yet), `rekey_pending_bucket_to` returns false and the caller falls through to the existing drop path with `sdk_message_dropped` log. cwd-based disambiguation is a v2 concern. The primary single-spawn case is fully resolved.

body:
## Summary

Adds three filter flags to `mchammer-pt-stitch` for narrowing which windows feed into `stitch_entropy`:

- `--windows IDX[,IDX...]`: keep only the listed 0-based window indices (energy-sorted ascending). Convenience for "drop this window" without looking up its energy bounds.
- `--emin E_MIN` / `--emax E_MAX`: drop bins outside the range from each surviving window's entropy DataFrame *before* stitching, so the overlap-alignment step sees only the kept bins. A window with no bins after trim is silently dropped.

The flags compose: a window contributes iff it survives `--windows` AND has at least one bin after the `--emin`/`--emax` trim.

When any filter is active, the success line gains a `; kept K of W windows: (lo, hi), ...` suffix listing the survivors. When filters reduce a discovered run from >=2 windows down to fewer than 2 surviving, the CLI exits with a distinct error naming the active flags and the surviving windows, separate from the existing "needs at least two distinct windows" discovery-time error.

## Motivation

Pairs with the equal-area coexistence-point estimator landed in #32. The low-energy windows of a REWL run are often the hardest to converge and contribute the noisiest part of the stitched DOS, while the equal-area condition only cares about the inter-peak region of P(E|T_c). Trimming at stitch time keeps those windows out of the alignment step rather than carrying them through to the coexistence finder.

body:
## Summary

Two operator-reported bugs from the latest E2E pipeline session, plus codex review follow-ups.

### Bug 5 — workflow_snapshot misses recovery descendants

The operator's heartbeat polls \`workflow_snapshot\` to see the state of an in-flight workflow chain. The recursive CTE walked \`parent_task_id\` only, so rework tasks (spawned by \`create_rework_task\`) — which inherit the failed task's parent (NOT pointing back to the failed task) — were invisible from a snapshot rooted at the failed task. Orphan reworks (parent NULL or outside chain) were invisible from any root.

Fix: extend CTE to walk BOTH \`parent_task_id\` and \`previous_task_id\` edges; \`IN (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM chain)\` dedupes the rare two-edge case. Each rework stage now surfaces \`previous_task_id\` so the operator can identify lineage without an extra \`get_task\` call.

Critically, \`chain_breaks_24h\` and \`terminal_without_children\` semantic UNCHANGED — a rework is a retry of the same stage, not a downstream handoff, and counts as a chain break. Pinned by the existing \`test_previous_task_id_chain_does_not_suppress_chain_break\`.

### Bug 2 — chat assistant messages disappeared mid-tool

Two distinct gaps remained after PR #957's partial-write fix:

**(A) Server-side**: \`_chat_inner\` and \`_chat_stream_inner\` exception handlers (LLMAuthError / LLMConfigError / generic Exception) and tool-loop terminate paths called \`append_chat_message(\"assistant\", msg)\` without \`turn_id\`. The earlier \`partial=True\` entry stayed orphaned on disk next to a separate \"Error: ...\" / \"Stopped: ...\" bubble.

Fix: new \`_finalize_chat_turn\` helper writes ONE final entry sharing the partial's \`turn_id\` with content = \`<accumulated text>\\n\\n<closing>\`. \`load_chat_transcript\`'s dedupe replaces the partial cleanly. Used at all 8 abnormal-close sites (3 exception × 2 functions + 1 terminate × 2). Helper rejects empty \`turn_id\` with ValueError so a future refactor can't silently regress to the orphaned-partial bug.

**(B) Client-side**: WS reconnect handler in app.js cleared \`_chatFetchedAt\` but \`_loadChatHistory\` still early-returned because \`chatStreamingAgents[id]\` was stuck true (set on text_delta, cleared only on chat_done — the disconnect ate the chat_done). Reset all per-agent ephemeral chat-stream state on reconnect — BUT guard the wipe per-agent against active local SSE streams: \`_chatAborts[id]\` is the AbortController for the in-flight \`/chat/stream\` fetch, and wiping it mid-stream would kill our handle on the local render target.

### Codex review notes addressed

- P1: WS reconnect now skips agents with active local SSE streams (per-agent guard on both the state wipe AND the refetch loop).
- P2: \`_finalize_chat_turn\` requires a non-empty \`turn_id\` (raises ValueError otherwise).
- P2: server.py \`/mesh/tasks/workflow/{root_task_id}\` docstring updated to mention previous_task_id traversal.

## Test plan

- [x] 6 new tests pinning workflow_snapshot rework discovery (failed-task root, kickoff root, multi-step chain, dedup, orphan parent, terminal-flag preservation)
- [x] 7 new tests pinning _finalize_chat_turn helper behavior and the end-to-end wiring through _chat_inner's LLMConfigError path and _chat_stream_inner's generic Exception path
- [x] 1 new test for empty-turn_id rejection
- [x] Existing \`test_previous_task_id_chain_does_not_suppress_chain_break\` still passes (semantic preserved)
- [x] Full suite: 6448 passed, 49 skipped, 0 failures
- [x] Ruff clean
- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger an SEO-pipeline E2E where validator fails → confirm rework surfaces in workflow_snapshot rooted at the failed validator
- [ ] Manual smoke: send chat message that triggers a long blocking tool, drop WS mid-tool, verify the in-flight bubble persists and resumes after reconnect

Currently, the `KubernetesRuntime` hardcodes the Kubernetes service domain suffix to `.svc.cluster.local` when constructing the gRPC address used by the Function Worker to connect to function

author: jfmeyers
body:
## Summary

- Adds `pl`, `tr`, `sv`, `cs`, `zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `hi` to `KnownSamples` in `TrigramLanguageDetectorTests`. Empirical end-to-end coverage grows from **7 → 15 Granit base cultures**, matching the framework's localization surface.
- `Iso639Map` now folds the three Hindi-belt Bihari languages (Magahi `mag`, Bhojpuri `bho`, Maithili `mai`) to `hi`. Without this, modern formal Hindi prose scores closest to Franc's Magahi profile and the detector returns `null`. None of these have an ISO 639-1 code, none are part of the Granit base-culture surface, and Postgres ships only the Hindi stemmer for Devanagari — so folding to `hi` matches both framework coverage and downstream stemming/indexing reality. Rationale documented inline in [Iso639Map.cs](src/Granit.LanguageDetection.Trigram/Internal/Iso639Map.cs).
- README coverage section updated.

## Notes

- Polish/Czech/Swedish/Turkish exercise the Latin multi-language profile path.
- Chinese/Japanese/Korean hit single-language script shortcuts in `ScriptDetector`.
- Hindi exercises the Devanagari multi-language profile path (with the macro-language folding above).
- Turkish initially failed on the short suggested sample — lengthened to ~3 sentences with characteristic constructs (`ı/İ`, `ş`, `ğ`).

Closes #2294.
